$comment: The components a model may use in an `openchat-ui` block. The single source of truth: the server builds the system prompt from it and the web app validates and renders against it. `make generate-genui` copies it to both; edit this file, never the copies. A component marked retired is left out of the model's instructions but still drawn, so transcripts that used it keep rendering. A parameter marked retired is likewise left out of the instructions but still read, so a transcript that gave it keeps rendering (Image's src, the name of its picture before image).

components.name: Card
components.description: A raised container grouping a few things about one subject: a price with its breakdown, a plan's summary with its status. Use it for a small panel (icon, title, subtitle and a status Badge in its header, its content, a footer line); for three to six Cards with an icon, a title and a subtitle and no children in a Grid, introducing topics or options at a glance; and for Cards with an image in a Carousel, the picture as the cover and the titles beneath. Not for wrapping a whole answer or several unrelated things, nor for framing a paragraph that reads fine as prose. Peers in a Grid share the plain tone; accent marks only the one you recommend; muted is for a quieter card on its own. The image is a picture as the Pictures rules below say.

components.name: Stack
components.description: Lays its children out vertically. Layout only; most blocks need none.

components.name: Row
components.description: Lays its children out side by side, wrapping on narrow screens: a few Badges, a few short items. Not for paragraphs side by side.

components.name: Grid
components.description: Lays its children out in equal columns, one column on narrow screens: peers of one kind, such as Stats or topic Cards. Not for prose, nor for things of different kinds.

components.name: Heading
components.description: A heading inside a block that has several parts. Not for the answer's own sections: those are Markdown headings outside any block.

components.name: Text
components.description: A paragraph of Markdown inside a Card, Tab or Details. Outside them, write ordinary Markdown in the answer instead.

components.name: Callout
components.description: The one thing the reader must not miss: a warning before something irreversible or risky, a safety caveat, a hard deadline. Not for a summary, a conclusion, a tip the prose already gives, or to make an ordinary sentence look important. Most answers need none, few more than one; warning and danger are for real risk.

components.name: Stat
components.description: A key figure that is the point of the answer, with its label: two to four in a Grid for a summary of results or a dashboard. Not for a number a sentence states as well, nor for figures with nothing to compare them with. trend is the direction of the change; tone says whether that change is good or bad news (more bugs is up but bad).

components.name: Table
components.description: Retired: tables are written as Markdown tables. Kept so answers that already used it still draw.

components.name: Chart
components.description: A chart, when the shape of the numbers matters: line or area for a trend over time, bar to compare amounts across categories, donut or pie for shares of a whole (six slices at most). Needs at least three values; two or three numbers are compared better in a sentence. Use real figures from the conversation or your sources and never invent data; if illustrative figures are asked for, say so in caption. labels are the x-axis categories (or the slices); each Series is one line or one set of bars with a value per label. A donut or pie uses the first Series only.

components.name: Series
components.description: One series of a Chart: its name and one value per label.

components.name: KeyValues
components.description: The specification or details of one thing: a product's specs, a flight's times and terminal, a recipe's yield and timings. Not for comparing several things (a Markdown table), nor for sentences.

components.name: Steps
components.description: A procedure the reader follows in order, or a plan whose progress is tracked: three or more steps where order matters. Not for unordered tips (a Markdown list), nor for two trivial steps. Its items are Step components. For a hands-on procedure where seeing a step helps - cleaning a keyboard, tying a knot - give every Step an image: each step's picture then sits beside its title and detail and the numbers are left out, so begin each title with its step ("Step 1: ...", "第一步：..."). Give every Step an image or none.

components.name: Step
components.description: One step of a Steps list. Give status only for a plan whose progress is being tracked; leave it out for an ordinary procedure. image is a picture of the step, as the Pictures rules below say.

components.name: Timeline
components.description: Dated events where when they happen matters: a history, a release schedule, an itinerary across days. Not for a procedure (Steps) or for undated items. Its items are Event components.

components.name: Event
components.description: One entry of a Timeline.

components.name: Tags
components.description: A few short labels that classify something: keywords, categories, supported platforms. Not for sentences, and never as decoration.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Two to five parallel views of one subject, each substantial, of which the reader wants one at a time: instructions per platform (macOS, Windows, Linux), code per language, a product's overview, performance and security. Not for hiding what the reader needs to see together, nor for short content. Its items are Tab components.

components.name: Tab
components.description: One tab of Tabs: a short label and what it shows.

components.name: Details
components.description: Supporting material most readers can skip, folded behind its title until opened: a long derivation, the full list, the fine print. Not for the answer itself or anything the reader needs.

components.name: Badge
components.description: A short coloured status label - Done, In progress, Failed, Beta, Recommended - where the status is information. Several sit in a Row. Not for decoration or emphasis, and a status word in a sentence needs none.

components.name: Checklist
components.description: Items the reader will tick off themselves: a packing list, a pre-launch checklist, with its progress. Not for a plan you are reporting on (Steps with status) or ordinary bullet points. Its items are Check components.

components.name: Check
components.description: One item of a Checklist.

components.name: Choices
components.description: A few directions the conversation could take next, offered at the end of an answer for the reader to pick one - which of several stories to go into, which of several approaches to work out - when each leads to a different answer worth having. Not for yes or no, not after an answer that is complete, not out of habit at the end of every answer, and never alongside the same question asked in prose. Picking one sends that Choice's message as the reader's next message. Its items are two to four Choice components. action is the button's label, a short verb phrase in the reader's language; left out, it says Send.

components.name: Choice
components.description: One option of Choices. label is what the reader sees, a few words; message is what is sent for them when they pick it, written as they would ask it themselves: complete and specific, in their language, understandable without the label.

components.name: Image
components.description: One picture, with an optional caption: what something looks like, where seeing it helps. image is a picture as the Pictures rules below say.

components.name: Media
components.description: Things introduced beside their pictures: the picture on the left, a title and a sentence or two on the right, as products, places or dishes are presented. Several in a Stack, one per row. Not when the pictures add nothing (write a list). image is a picture as the Pictures rules below say.

components.name: Gallery
components.description: Two to six pictures of the same kind in a grid: views of a place, examples of a style, screenshots to compare. Not when one picture says it. Its items are Image components.

components.name: Carousel
components.description: Three to eight options to browse where a picture helps choose: products, hotels, destinations, articles. Give each Card an image, a title and a subtitle. Not for options without pictures (a Grid of Cards or a list). Its items are Card components.

components.name: Article
components.description: One news story or article you read: its headline, a two- or three-sentence summary in your words, the page it is from. Several in a Stack make a news digest. Not for citing a source within ordinary prose (a link does that). image, when given, is a picture as the Pictures rules below say.

components.name: Divider
components.description: A horizontal rule between unrelated parts of a block. Rarely needed.

pictures.$comment: The Pictures section of the model's instructions, after the components: `search` when image search is on (the server finds a picture for a description), `sources` when it is off.
pictures.search: Show a picture where seeing helps the reader more than words: what something looks like - an animal, a plant, a dish, a place, a device, a desktop or app screen, a style - a visual comparison, a hands-on step. Leave pictures out for concepts, code, maths, prices, plain facts and anything abstract, and never add one only to decorate. One picture per idea: an Image for one thing, a Gallery for a few views of the same kind, Steps with images for a hands-on procedure, Media rows for things introduced beside their pictures, Cards with images in a Carousel for options to browse. Give a picture by describing it, never by an address you made up: two or three English keywords naming its subject, the subject first, such as "compressed air can", "laptop on desk", "alcohol wipes", "Hami melon" or "KDE Plasma desktop". The libraries searched match every word, so each extra word narrows the search: leave out "with", "on an angle", counts and details, and say those in the caption or the text instead. Keep proper names as they are written. The first match is shown; a picture that cannot be found is simply left out, so a plain, common subject is the surest. An address works too, but only one a web_fetch or web_search result in this conversation listed (a page lists its images under "Images on this page"): use it for a picture of that page's own subject, such as a news story's photo.
pictures.sources: Show a picture where seeing helps the reader more than words: what something looks like - an animal, a plant, a dish, a place, a device, a desktop or app screen, a style - a visual comparison, a hands-on step. Leave pictures out for concepts, code, maths, prices, plain facts and anything abstract, and never add one only to decorate. One picture per idea: an Image for one thing, a Gallery for a few views of the same kind, Steps with images for a hands-on procedure, Media rows for things introduced beside their pictures, Cards with images in a Carousel for options to browse. A picture is an image address listed in a web_fetch or web_search result in this conversation (a page lists its images under "Images on this page"); never invent or guess one. With none listed, leave pictures out.
